newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on Cargill, short covering, CBT.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on Cargill, short covering, CBT.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on Cargill demand, commission and local short covering and firm CBOT soycomplex values, traders said.

"Cargill was the best buyer of the July with UGG selling, locals and commission short covering of the May," a trader said. July WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -16.32 Thursday from -17.46 Wednesday. July-Nov spread at $49, May-July $4.70, Sep-Nov $4.50. Volume was 3,415 lots with 210 hedge lots.
Japan bought 4,000-5,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
May canola rose $1.20 to $419.40/tonne, July up $1.40 at $424.30 and November up $1.20 at $374.60.
May flax lost $3.20 to $343.80, July down $2.90 to $341.10 after commission sell stops were triggered at $343. May-July $1.50. Volume was 420 lots with 55 hedges.

May western barley rose $1 to $140.60 as commercials bought from PCTS, October up $0.70 to $139.70 on commercials. Alberta Wheat Pool sold May-July barley at $0.50, traders said. Volume was 1,175 lots.
May feed wheat rose $1 to $171 and July rose $1 to $168.50 on LFG demand, trader said. Volume was 1,005 lots.
PCTS sold May feed pea contracts steady at US$217 to RBC-DS, traders said. Volume was 25 lots.
LFG bought May oats up US$2 to US$126, October down US$0.50 at US$123.50 and opened March at US$126, traders said. Volume 65.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas, oats)
